Name: Threatening Self-Harm to Control

Name: Free Riding

Name: Sabotaging Your Employment

Name: Withholding Basic Resources

Name: Damages Your Social or Business Relationships

Name: Threatening with or Brandishing Weapons

Name: Invasive Snooping

Name: Over-monitoring Your Life

Name: Destroying Your Possessions

Name: Weaponizing the Legal System

Name: Sabotaging Work or School Commitments

Name: Subjecting You to Sleep Deprivation

Name: Stalking

Name: Breaking Things in Rage

Name: Disrupting Social Bonds

Name: Frequently Sabotages Your Social Plans

Name: Undermines Your Social Connections

Name: Jealousy Induction

Name: Pathological Altruism

Example: Prioritizing others to the extent that their own needs are consistently dismissed.

Name: Avoids Future-Oriented Conversations

Example: When you mention planning a vacation together months ahead, they change the subject or say, "Let's see when the time comes.”

Name: Ghosts or Disengages Without Explanation

Example: After weeks of daily interaction, they suddenly stop responding to messages and calls, leaving you confused and hurt.

Name: Withdraws When Closeness Increases

Name: Conditional Affection
Definition: They set conditional terms for commitment, suggesting you need to change to be worthy.
Example: They imply, "I'd consider us serious if you lost some weight," making you feel inadequate.

Name: Says One Thing, Does Another

Example: In front of friends, they refer to you as their partner, but in private, they dismiss the label, saying, "Let's not get ahead of ourselves.”

Name: Overly Dependent on Your Presence

Name: Demands Constant Companionship
Definition: The individual desires constant companionship, feeling uneasy or insecure when apart from their partner.
Example: Becoming upset or anxious when the partner makes independent plans, expressing a need to share all leisure time together to feel secure in the relationship.

Name: Loses Self in Relationship
Definition: The individual sacrifices their hobbies and friendships to dedicate all attention to the partner, often to avoid perceived threats to the relationship.
Example: Giving up a beloved weekly sports activity because it conflicts with the partner's schedule, aiming to align completely with the partner's routines and interests.

Name: Financially Dependent on You

Example: Frequently asking the partner to cover expenses or manage financial decisions, expressing discomfort or avoidance when discussing personal budgeting or contributions.

Name: Resents Your Solo Activities
Definition: Feeling uneasy or threatened when the partner engages in activities without them, fearing it may lead to growing apart.
Example: Reacting with jealousy or anxiety when the partner plans a night out with friends, questioning the partner's commitment or expressing fears of being left out.

Name: Fear-Driven Attention-Seeking

Example: Regularly seeking verbal reassurances of love and commitment, and feeling distressed or engaging in people-pleasing behaviors if the partner seems even slightly distant.

Name: Unpredictable Behavior Patterns (Hot and cold, shifting narratives, erratic behavior)

Name: Feeding the Weeds

Name: Disregard for Laws and Social Norms

Example: Regularly participating in theft, vandalism, or other criminal acts without concern for consequences.

Name: Unaccountability

Example: Expressing indifference after defrauding a family member, with no intention of making amends.
